en: The Ritual Manual for the Contemplative Practice of Bhaisajyaguru Tathāgata, in one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India.
First, the three prostrations; next, the confession, receiving the precepts, and the bodhicitta; next, the service of the mantra.
After reciting this seven times, the Buddha performs the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) and offers this verse of invocation to Mahācakra-vajra:
I prostrate to the Great Flower-toothed One of the supreme seal, To the Mysterious Trace (*Guhyakādhipati*),
the Great Wheel-King, To Acala, Ucchuṣma, and the Fire-head, And to Kārttikeya who binds the boundaries.
Whether manifesting wrath or laughter with fierce anger, he shifts mountains and turns the oceans in an instant;
he subdues the rakshasas and their poisonous minds, and upon hearing the recitation of the mantra, they are all struck with terror.
He annihilates the ten non-virtues and transforms all sentient beings, transcending to enter the ocean of the Tathagata’s merit.
To protect the disciples who maintain the recitation, you have resolved to grant your praise and response upon being invoked.
O Great Vajra Pure Assembly, may the vajra scepter always follow you;
at this site of the ritual arena for worship and recitation, surround it on all sides and perform the boundary-binding.
Next is the Great Wheel Seal (*mahācakra-mudrā*): interlace the left and right hands within the palms, with both thumbs also inserted into the palms.
Place this seal upon the crown of the head.
Place the left foot upon the right knee,
recite [the mantra] twenty-one times,
then lower it, embrace it, and scatter it.

Namo bhagavate aparājitāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ vīra vīra mahākālabhañjari | Sata sata | Śaraṇe | Trāye trāye | Vidhamani | Samparśani | Trailokye | Siddhāritaloke | Svāhā || Note: Where there is a half-syllable (ardhamātra) indicated by a dot above, it must be read with the preceding vowel. Where there is a conjunct consonant (saṃyoga), the first syllable must be pronounced as a half-syllable and joined with the following "a" sound. When a half-syllable occurs, it must be recited with the "prolonged" (pluta) tone. Recite this dhāraṇī twenty-seven times.
One should immediately enter all maṇḍalas— herein referred to as *tán* (altars)—
and then contemplate and observe that all sentient beings are by nature pure.
Obscured by adventitious defilements, one does not awaken to True Suchness (tathatā). Therefore,
these three secrets of empowerment (adhiṣṭhāna) are taught,
so that both oneself and others may attain purity.
Then, with the two hands joined in the lotus-anjali gesture,
recite the mantra for purifying the three karmas three times.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ svabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāva-śūnyatā. Then, enter the hall.
Furthermore, if one wishes to enter the chamber of the Honored One,
one should first gaze upon the Honored One’s countenance and join the ten fingers in palms-pressed salutation.
One should keep one's head bowed.
Whenever entering the practice hall,
stand upright with the body aligned facing the Honzon.
With palms joined like a lotus and eyes closed,
direct the mind to imagine yourself before a certain Tathāgata and his retinue of bodhisattvas in a particular world;
then prostrate yourself with the five limbs touching the ground.
Visualize that you are respectfully prostrating before each and every Buddha and Bodhisattva.
Then, recite the Universal Prostration Mantra: *Oṃ sarvatathāgatapraṇāmanamaskāre*. Immediately thereafter, perform the ritual action accordingly.
Having recited the names of the Buddhas and so forth,
next, place your right knee on the ground and join your palms at your heart.

With sincere devotion, one confesses and repents all karmic obstacles and transgressions from beginningless time, and then rejoices in all the meritorious deeds cultivated by the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all sentient beings.
Furthermore, he contemplates all the Tathāgatas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who have attained equal and perfect enlightenment and are turning the wheel of Dharma;
he contemplates all the Tathāgatas who manifest parinirvāṇa,
as well as those who remain long in the world without entering parinirvāṇa.
Furthermore, he made this vow:
"By whatever roots of goodness I have accumulated through prostrating to the Buddhas, repenting, requesting [the turning of the wheel], and rejoicing [in merit],"
Dedicate this mass of merit to all sentient beings,
vowing that they may all enter the secret treasury of the three virtues.
Next is the text for repentance.
I take refuge in the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the ten directions, the Supreme Dharma, and the Assembly of Bodhisattvas.
With the pure actions of body, speech, and mind, I reverently join my palms in homage.
Whatever sins have been produced by the actions of body, speech, and mind throughout the beginningless cycle of existence, [I now confess].
Just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have performed repentance, so do I now set forth my repentance in the same manner.
Next is the text for rejoicing:
With a heart now deeply inspired by joy, I rejoice in all accumulations of merit and wisdom.
I rejoice in all the roots of virtue accumulated by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas within their practices and vows, those born from the three vajra actions,
as well as by the Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all sentient beings.
[Next is the text for the Request:]
All you Lamps of the World seated at the site of enlightenment, Whose awakened eyes are blossomed and illuminate the three realms—
I now kneel and first entreat you To turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma. All Tathāgatas,
lords of the triple world, Who are about to enter parinirvāṇa without remainder:
I exhort them all to remain for a long time, Not forsaking their compassionate vows to save the world.
Next, I pray for the dedication of merit:
May the merit from repentance, sympathetic joy, and exhortation Cause me never to lose the bodhicitta.
Among the sublime assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, you are ever a virtuous friend, never wearying of or abandoning them;
born free from the eight difficulties, your body is adorned with the wisdom of recollecting past lives;
far removed from delusion, you possess both compassion and wisdom, and are fully able to fulfill the pāramitās.
Born into noble lineages, with abundant wealth, joy, and prosperity, Surrounded by vast retinues that are ever-thriving,
Possessing the four unhindered analytical knowledges and ten masteries, With the six supernormal powers and all meditative absorptions fully perfected—
Just as with Vajradhvaja and Samantabhadra, May my praise and dedication likewise be so.
Next, generate the mind of samādhi; next, [enter] the samaya of the Buddha Family; next, assume the full lotus posture (paryaṅka), or the half-lotus posture with the right leg over the left.
Anoint the hands with incense.
Form the Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Family:
join the two hands with palms hollowed and fingers interlaced;
extend the two index fingers and slightly bend them.
Place each [thumb] upon the proximal phalanx of the middle finger.
Then, open both thumbs and pinch the first joint of the lower part of each index finger.
Having completed the mudrā,
visualize the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics of the Buddha [Name] clearly.
Then, recite the Heart Samaya Mantra of the Buddha Family, which says:
Oṃ tathāgatādya-nābhavya svāhā. Recite this three times or seven times.
Having placed it upon the crown of the head,
one disperses it; by forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra,
all the holy assemblies of the Buddha family are awakened.
All [deities] empower and protect those who practice the true mantras,
swiftly causing them to attain purity of physical action, the eradication of karmic obstacles, and the increase of merit and wisdom.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family.
Join the two hands with palms hollowed and held together.
Touch the tips of the two thumbs and the two little fingers to one another.
Slightly bend the remaining fingers so that they resemble the shape of a blooming lotus flower.
One then forms this mudrā.
Having bound the mudrā,
one visualizes the physical marks and signs of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva as being perfectly majestic and dignified.
Surrounded by an immeasurable *koṭi* of retinues belonging to the Lotus family, one should recite the Samaya-mantra of the Lotus family as follows:
*Oṃ padmanātha svāhā*. Recite this three or seven times to perform the consecration (*adhiṣṭhāna*).
Place the seal at the crown of the head and then disperse it to the right;
by forming this seal and reciting the mantra,
one awakens Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the holy assembly of the Lotus Family.
All of them come to empower the practitioner,
whereby one attains purity of verbal karma;
one's speech becomes majestic and solemn, causing others to delight in hearing it.
Possessing unimpeded eloquence and mastery in preaching the Dharma,
one next binds the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family:
with both hands, the left inverted and the right upright, join the backs of the palms together.
Interlace the right thumb with the left little finger and the left thumb with the right little finger;
the six middle fingers are pressed flat against the wrists.
The form of a three-pronged vajra is thus completed.
Form the mudrā at the heart and visualize the physical marks,
secondary signs, and majestic radiance of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha.
Surrounded by an immeasurable retinue of Vajradharas, one should then recite the Samaya-mantra of the Vajra Family:
Oṃ vajranābhāya svāhā. Recite this three or seven times to perform the consecration.
Place the seal at the crown of the head and then disperse it to the left.
By forming this seal and reciting the mantra,
one awakens the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha and the assembly of deities of the Vajra Family.
All of them come to empower the practitioner,
who thereby attains purity of mental action, realizes the bodhicitta,
manifests samādhi, and swiftly achieves liberation.
Next, regarding the *mudrā* and mantra for the *Muṇḍarī* incense burner: recite the *hṛdaya-mantra* twenty-one times; thereafter, burn the incense, and all shall rejoice.

Next, regarding the *mudrā* and mantra for the *Muṇḍarī* scented water: if one uses various flowers, powdered incense, and so forth, having performed this *mudrā* and consecrated them with the mantra, place the water before the Buddha, and all shall rejoice.
Next, take up the incense burner and offer this invocation:
"To the Tathāgatas of the Seven Buddhas of the East,
and to all Buddhas throughout the ten directions."
The Bodhisattvas of the Eight Great Offerings and the Four Means of Attraction;
the great Bodhisattvas such as Sūryaprabha and Candraprabha; and all Bodhisattvas.
All the Vajra-devas, nāgas, spirits, and the twelve divine generals,
each with seven thousand yakṣa deities and all the various deities of the paths of karma, have fully witnessed and known this.
I now request this ground as my own territory.
Upon this ground, I shall establish for seven days and seven nights the dharma-gate of the maṇḍala ritual site of the Buddha [Name].
All the great Bodhisattvas, all the Vajra deities,
and their respective retinues, please bear witness to my accomplishment.
I now wish to perform the rites for protecting the body and binding the boundaries.
In this very land, throughout the east,
west, south, north, the four intermediate directions,
and above and below, all those piśācas, yakṣas, evil spirits, ghosts, and others who destroy the Buddha-dharma—
They all departed to a distance of seven li;
as for the protective deities, spirits,
and others who serve the Buddha-dharma and bring benefit to it within the Buddha-dharma, they remained.
One should then abide in the seven protection-of-the-body dharma-seal mantras known as the "Three Whites.
Next, form the Vajra Armor Protection-of-the-Body Seal:
interlace the two little fingers and the two ring fingers with the right over the left.
The two middle fingers are held straight and vertical with their tips touching;
the two index fingers are bent into the shape of hooks and placed against the backs of the middle fingers without touching them.
Join the two thumbs upright and press them against the ring fingers; thus the mudrā is formed.
Place the mudrā at the heart and recite the mantra.
Recite it once for each of the five locations of the body.
First seal the forehead;
next, seal the right shoulder;
next, seal the left shoulder.
Next, seal the heart;
next, seal the throat.
These constitute the five locations.
Immediately, one gives rise to a mind of great loving-kindness,
universally taking all sentient beings as its object,
and makes the aspiration that they all be adorned with the armor of great compassion.
May they swiftly be freed from all obstacles and hindrances, and realize the supreme accomplishments of both the mundane and supramundane realms.
Having contemplated thus, one immediately dons the adamantine armor;
no demons whatsoever will dare to create obstacles or hindrances.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajragītipratiṣṭhāya svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, through the power of a compassionate heart and sympathetic concern, [the desired result is attained].
All celestial Māras and various obstructing spirits see the practitioner’s majestic radiance blazing forth like the solar disc;
each gives rise to a heart of loving-kindness and is unable to create obstacles.
Furthermore, wicked people will be unable to find an opportunity [to harm them];
their bodies will not be defiled by the karmic obstructions of afflictions,
and they will also be protected from the sufferings of the evil realms in the future.
May I swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi.
Next, I pray for protection while taking up the incense burner;
I, [Name], now address the Buddhas of the ten directions, all the *prajñāpāramitās*, and all the great bodhisattvas.
May all the Bodhisattvas Avalokiteśvara,
all the Bodhisattvas Vajragarbha, and all the heavenly beings, nāgas,
and the eight classes of spirits— the various virtuous divine kings who protect the stūpas and the Dharma— bear witness.
I, the bhikṣu [Name], for the purpose of upholding the Buddha-dharma and performing those tasks, request your grace and protection so that all may be accomplished as desired.
Having thus prayed for initial protection, one should circumambulate clockwise from the northeast corner.
Next, recite the mantra of the *Muṇḍarī* ritual for expelling *vināyakas* twenty-one times.
Then, for the *Dharani for Subduing the Earth*, recite the *Sarvakarmika-mantra* together with the *Mahācitta-mantra* of *Muṇḍarī* seven times.
The mantra for sprinkling the boundaries of the site, which can remove all impurities and bring about purity in all matters:
Oṃ hūṃ kuruḍana huṃ phaṭ. Next is the mudrā and mantra for the horse-headed (Hayagrīva) protection of the body and the delimitation of the boundary.
From the middle fingers of both hands,
extend the three fingers outward and interlace them; then,
with each hand flat against the back of the other, join the palms together.
The two index fingers are held straight up,
separated by about five *aṅgula*,
with both thumbs touching them.
Bend each finger joint once;
do not let them touch the tips of the index fingers.
The mantra for coming and going is as follows:
Oṃ pravicāsitā vajra śvārārci svāhā. This is the dharmamudrā mantra.
If one wishes to receive and uphold this Bodhisattva Dharma,
one must first recite the mantra of this Dharma-seal.
Having protected oneself, one should further consecrate water seven times with the mantra.
Next, seal the water with the mudrā;
or alternatively, consecrate white mustard seeds or ashes with the mantra.
In each case, perform the sealing and recitation seven times.
Plant wooden stakes at the four corners and scatter mustard seed ash-water in the ten directions; thus the boundary is established.
Thereafter, all ritual practices performed shall be efficacious. Next follows the Mudrā and Dhāraṇī of the Single-Syllable King-Conquering Vajra Cundā.
Next, form the mudrā of the vajra-kila for binding the boundary of the earth.
First, insert the middle finger of the right hand between the left index and middle fingers;
then, insert the right ring finger between the left ring and little fingers.
With both hands extended outward,
wrap the left middle finger around the back of the right middle finger and insert it between the tips of the right thumb and middle finger.
Wrap the left ring finger around the back of the right ring finger;
insert [the left ring finger] between the right ring finger and little finger.
Place the tips of the two little fingers and the two index fingers against each other.
By interlocking the two thumbs beneath [the palms],
the seal is formed. Having bound this seal,
visualize it in the shape of a vajra.
Touch the ground with the two thumbs;
recite the mantra once and perform the mudrā once upon the ground.
Repeating this three times, a firm adamantine seat (*vajrāsana*) is established.
The mantra of the earth element:
Oṃ kili kili vajravajri bhūruṇḍa bhūṇḍa hūṃ phaṭ. Having formed this mudrā, recite the mantra to perform the consecration.
Extending downward to the limit of the vajra-circle, it forms an indestructible vajra-boundary that even the most powerful māras cannot shake;
with little exertion of effort, one attains great accomplishment.
All impure and foul things within the earth become entirely purified through the power of empowerment;
that realm is established according to the size one intends in one's mind.
Next, form the Vajra Wall mudrā.
Following the previous earth-boundary mudrā, open the palms and extend the two thumbs upward, standing like a wall; thus it is accomplished.
Visualize blazing flames flowing forth from the mudrā.
Rotate the mudrā clockwise around the body three times;
as you recite the aforementioned earth-element mantra, it becomes a wall and boundary of adamantine solidity.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarasara vajraprakāra hūṃ phaṭ. By means of binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra, as well as through the power of contemplative practice (bhāvanā), [the obstacles are bound].
According to the size of one's intention, one forms a square boundary wall of vajra-light and flames;
no demons, evil persons, tigers, wolves, lions, or venomous insects can approach it.
Next, the Great Body-Protection Mudrā of Cundā is used to seal the four directions and the four gates.
The ritual procedures are all accomplished.

Next is the Great Wrathful Dharma-Body Seal of Kuntali; next is the Great Demon-Subduing Dharma-Body Seal of Kuntali; next is the Great Three-Eyed Dharma-Body Seal of Kuntali; then, bind the seal of the Bodhisattva Mahāgaganagañja.
Join the two hands in *añjali*.
Interlace the two middle fingers so that the right presses upon the left from the outside,
with the palms touching the backs of the hands.
By pressing the two index fingers together in the shape of a jewel, the mudrā is formed.
Visualize that from this seal, immeasurable articles of offering—such as clothing, food, drink, palaces, and multi-storied pavilions—stream forth.
As explained extensively in the *Yogācārabhūmi*, one recites the mantra as follows:
Oṃ gaganasvabhāvavajra hūṃ. Thus, the practitioner [should recite].
Even if one's power of visualization is weak,
by virtue of the empowering force of this mudrā and mantra,
all offering substances become truly real.
Just as in the world-system of such-and-such a person who performs vast offerings,
one next visualizes within the maṇḍala the syllable *kṛ* (pronounced *kṛ-i*) with a long vowel, emitting great light in the color of red crystal.
It shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Any sentient being within those realms who encounters this light shall have all their karmic obstructions and hindrances completely extinguished.
Next, form the Tathāgata Fist Seal: clench the four fingers of the left hand into a fist and extend the thumb straight upward;
with the right hand, form a vajra-fist.
Grasp the left thumb and it is immediately accomplished.
With this mudrā, seal the ground and recite the mantra seven times to empower it.
To transform the world, the Tathāgata-muṣṭi mantra is as follows:
Oṃ ekapada-praveśa khaṃ. By the power of the blessing conferred by forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the world is transformed].
He immediately transforms this trichiliocosm into the buddha-field of such-and-such a name,
with the seven treasures as its ground,
where the waterfowl, trees, and forests all proclaim the sounds of the Dharma.
The immeasurable adornments are as described in the sūtra.
Therein, he spoke these verses:
By the power of my merit, And by the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
And by the power of the dharma-realm, may they accomplish a land of peace and bliss;
for through the repeated practice of this samādhi and wisdom,
in their present life, they constantly abide within meditative concentration.
He beholds a certain Tathāgata named [Name] in a certain world,
amidst a great assembly of bodhisattvas, hearing him preach immeasurable sūtras;
at the time of his death, his mind is undisturbed and samādhi manifests before him.
In an instant, one will swiftly be born in that land and attain enlightenment through lotus-birth.
Next, bind the seal of the precious chariot: with both hands palms upturned and interlaced, place the right hand over the left.

Place the two index fingers side by side, touching each other, and press the two thumbs against the first joint below the two index fingers; this forms the seal. The mantra for dispatching the chariot is:
Oṃ tūru tūru hūṃ. By forming this seal, one invites [the deity] in.
Visualize the formation of a carriage adorned with the seven treasures;
go to such-and-such a world to invite such-and-such a Buddha, together with his retinue of bodhisattvas, to mount this carriage without dispersing this seal.
With the two thumbs directed toward the body,
one should flick the tips of the two middle fingers and then recite the mantra for requesting the chariot, which says:
*Namo siddhye svāhā*. (1) *Tathāgatāya namaḥ*. (2) *Oṃ vairocanīye svāhā*. (3) One should then visualize the chariot arriving at the site of practice and remaining suspended in mid-air.
Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the assembly of holy ones.
First, visualize the direction where the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Buddha resides and face that way;
then, invite that honored image.
Then, turning his body,
he placed the *śṛṅga* vessel before the honored image and crossed the eight fingers— beginning with the index fingers—
of both hands behind the palms, pressing the right over the left.
With the two wrists separated by about five inches,
move the two thumbs back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ hulu hulu canda li samudghe svāhā. First, join the palms together facing the original direction.
Then, with a heart of utmost sincerity, invoke those who are to be invited as follows:

Now, [I], so-and-so, for the sake of such-and-such matters, most reverently and with utmost sincerity invoke and entreat: Tathāgata King of Good Renown and Auspiciousness; Tathāgata Sovereign King of Jewel-Moon Wisdom-Adornment and Radiant Sound; Tathāgata Accomplishment of Golden-Colored Jewel-Light and Sublime Conduct; Tathāgata King of Griefless Supreme Auspiciousness; Tathāgata Thunderous Sound of the Dharma-Ocean; Tathāgata Playful Supernatural Power of Supreme Wisdom in the Dharma-Ocean; and Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaidūryaprabha. I pray to you all with a sincere heart again and again.

The petitioner addresses the Great Compassionate One: "I pray that you descend to this ritual site in accordance with your original vow. For the application of the Heart-Vajra-Seal of all Tathāgatas, as well as for all Tathāgatas, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattvas, Śakra, Brahmā, and all other devas, one should interlace the eight fingers of both hands, placing the right over the left."
Insert the hands into the palms and quickly close them into fists.

Extend both thumbs side by side and level, pressing down upon the middle joints of the right index fingers so that their tips do not bend, and so forth. If this seal is modified, the two thumbs move up and down together in tandem.
This is called the Seal of the Lineage of the Tathāgatas for Summoning. The mantra is:
Namo samantabuddhānām (1) Oṃ (2) Hūṃ (3) Irṇa (4). [Homage to] Bodhisattva Sūryaprabha and Bodhisattva Candraprabha.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva,
Gaganagañja Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva, and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
To the east [are] Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, Bodhisattva Vajramañjuśrī,
and Bodhisattva Ākarṣaṇasarvatathāgata.
To the South: Homage to the Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa of All Tathāgatas.
To the West: Homage to the Mahāsattva Sarvātathāgatāṅkuśa.
To the North: Homage to the Mahāsattva Sarvātathāgatasaṃgraha.
To the southeast is the Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatapriyadarśanaratnapūjā;
to the southwest is the Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatapriyadarśanaguhyapūjā;
to the northwest is the Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatagītapūjā.
The Bodhisattva of the Dance Offering of All Tathāgatas is in the northeast.
Above this, the Bodhisattva of the Incense Offering of All Tathāgatas is in the southeast.
The Bodhisattva of the Flower Offering of All Tathāgatas is in the southwest.
To the northwest is the Bodhisattva Offering Lamps to All Tathāgatas;
to the northeast is the Bodhisattva Offering Unguents to All Tathāgatas.
[These are] the Dharma Seals and Mantras of all Yakṣas.
With the four fingers of the right hand pointing downward,
hook the four fingers of the left hand;
the two thumbs are held upright and move back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kumbhīra svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra.
When constructing a great *maṇḍala* altar, [one should recite it].
Performing this mudrā and mantra, he summons [them] in for worship;
all are filled with joy.
General Piṅgala, General Vajrapāṇi.
General Micira, General Antira, General Anira, General Sandira, General Indara, General Paiyira.
General Mahura, General Jñāradra, General Caturdra, and General Vikara,
each respectfully entreats you.
The noble assembly of the Tathāgata, not forsaking their compassionate vows,
has come to this site of the maṇḍala— the pure land formed through samādhi—
along with immeasurable koṭis of great bodhisattvas.
Having received the offerings of the practitioners and realized the merit of accomplishment,
next, one should form the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva to perform the rites of expulsion and boundary-binding.
Join the two hands in *añjali*.
Bend the two index fingers and the two middle fingers into the palms so that they face each other’s backs.
Align the two thumbs, slightly bent, without touching the index fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ amṛtodbhava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Recite this three times.
Immediately, turning the mudrā three times to the left,
all māras are expelled and they all retreat and disperse of their own accord.
Turning the mudrā three times to the right, [the same occurs].
This immediately constitutes a firm and great boundary.
Next, bind the Vajrapāśa mudrā (Vajra-net seal),
following the procedure for the previous earth-boundary seal.
Form the seal by pressing the first joint of both index fingers with the two thumbs.
Recite the mantra three times;
as you recite, place the seal upon the crown of the head, rotate it clockwise, and then release it.
The mantra is: Oṃ viśvapādanarākṣa vajrapañjarā hūṃ phaṭ. By the power of this seal and the empowerment of this mantra, [the protection is established].
Immediately above, it is covered with a vajra net of adamantine solidity,
such that even the gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Emanations cannot obstruct or hinder it;
the practitioner’s body and mind become peaceful and blissful.
Samādhi will be easily accomplished.

Next, form the seal of the Vajra Fire Court Boundary (*vajrajvālāmaṇḍalabandhana-mudrā*): cover the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand so that they touch, and extend the two thumbs upward; thus it is formed.
Visualize that immeasurable flames of light flow forth from the mudrā.
Rotate the mudrā three times clockwise;
immediately, outside the vajra wall, there will be a surrounding encirclement of flames.
Thereby, the great boundary of firm, pure flames is established.
The mantra for establishing the boundary is:
Oṃ āḥ saṃgini hūṃ phaṭ. (4) Then, perform the mudrā for offering the *argha* perfumed water.

When placing the argha water, one should recite the mantra once for the largest [offering], seven times for the medium, and at least twenty-one times for the smallest. Regarding the ritual procedure for the argha: first, place both knees upon the ground.
One should place one's hands upon a ring of pure *kuśa* grass,
hold an *argha* vessel, and while burning incense, make this request:
"I pray that the Venerable One, by virtue of your original vow..."
Please descend to this ritual site.
We pray that you will look upon us with compassion and accept this argha water and these humble offerings.
With both left and right hands, hold the arghya vessel and offer it to the forehead;
recite the mantra three times while visualizing bathing the feet of the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra is: Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ gaganasamavasaraṇa svāhā. Then, offer the *argha* water for ablution.
It causes the practitioner’s three karmas to be purified,
washing away all afflictions, transgressions, and defilements,
from the stage of practice through conviction up to the ten stages and the Buddha stage.
When one realizes the perfection of these stages (*bhūmi-pāramitā*),
one receives the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) of the nectar-like Dharma-body (*amṛta-dharmakāya*) bestowed by all Tathāgatas.
Next, form the Flower Seat Seal (*puṣpa-āsana-mudrā*), following the previous Samaya Seal of the Lotus Family.
Slightly bending the fingers so they are perfectly rounded constitutes this mudrā.
Having bound this mudrā,
visualize that immeasurable vajra-lotuses flow forth from it.
Throughout this world-system named [Name],
may the Tathāgata named [Name] and all the great bodhisattvas and the entire assembly of noble ones each obtain this adamantine lotus flower as their seat.
The mantra is: Oṃ kamala svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra for empowerment, the practitioner attains the fulfillment of the ten stages (bhūmis).
One shall attain the vajra-seat;
the three karmas will become as firm as a vajra.
Having thus performed the invitation, one speaks these words:
Welcome, Venerable One!
Out of compassion for us, you have descended to this site of practice.
Furthermore, out of your gracious pity, please accept this humble offering by taking a seat here.
Again, with a sincere heart, he repeatedly prostrated himself and addressed the Venerable One, saying:
"Out of great compassion, please take pity on me and fulfill my original vow."
That [the deity] appears and descends is not within my power.
Recite the *Indrāṇī-dhāraṇī* of the Great Samaya Command three times. The command states:
"The boundary is bound by the samaya; the ritual deportment is fully perfected."
He requested the holy assembly to be seated according to the Dharma.
Then, at the western gate, he joined his palms, prostrated, knelt with reverence,
and held an incense burner while burning various famous incenses.
Visualize all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, and all the celestial deities;
likewise, the true Sambhogakāyas each move upon their seats and gaze upon the Buddha’s appearance as he preaches the Dharma.
Again, he spoke aloud to request the consecration of the boundary, saying:

"May all the noble assemblies each occupy their respective seats, remaining in full majestic deportment according to the Dharma. Having spoken these words, he scattered incense and took up a silver platter.
Taking various powdered incenses in both hands,
recite the Heart Mantra of the Universal Sovereign King of Uṣṇīṣas seven times over the incense powder.

From the inner court, scatter incense for the devas and others using the Samādhi Dhāraṇī of Incense; scatter flowers as before according to the method for powdered incense using the Samādhi Dhāraṇī of Flowers. At the beginning of the ritual, join the palms in prostration and offer a sincere expression of gratitude, saying:
I feel profound and great remorse that the incense, flowers, food, and drink now offered are for the most part not in accordance with the Dharma.
Next, when offering the unguent:
I make this vow: This incense is fragrant like the wondrous incense of the heavens; pure and protected, I now offer it to you.
I pray that you graciously accept it and cause my aspirations to be fulfilled.
The mantra for scented ointment (*vilepana*) is as follows: *āgare āgare sarvacchibhide burti svāhā*. Recite this mantra while applying the scented ointment.
Afterward, recite the mantra you maintain.
Purify it according to the Dharma and offer it to the Honored One.
By offering this incense, may I attain the five *dharmakāyas*.
May this flow forth from such [merit]: may these five stainless unguents polish and refine those tormented by heat;
may they seize and shatter all the hells, reaching even to the realms of scorching fire—thus one should offer these mantra-flowers.
He made this aspiration, saying:
"This flower is pure, and its place of origin is likewise pure. I now offer it;
I pray that you will graciously accept it and grant me accomplishment."
The mantra for offering flowers is as follows:
"By virtue of this flower offering, may I attain the thirty-two marks of a Great Man;
furthermore, may this merit be dedicated toward the realization of the wondrous enlightenment of the Flower Terrace."
May the radiance of light pervade and touch those in the realms of humans and devas who are intoxicated by the objects of desire,
and who are oppressed by the eight sufferings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven; may it awaken them all.
The Bodhicitta flourishes; may the constant bliss of Samantabhadra be attained.

I offer this incense—derived from forest trees and resinous gums—which can fulfill the aspirations of all beings. May the devas always partake of it; I now present this offering. Out of compassion, please accept it. The mantra for the offering of incense is as follows: [Mantra]
*Āgāra āgāra sarvabuddhaya dhara pudgati svāhā.* Recite this mantra over the incense.
Thereafter, recite the mantra you maintain;
offer incense to the sensory objects according to the ritual rules.
By virtue of my offering and burning of incense, may I attain the Buddha’s unimpeded wisdom,
be radiant with grace, and possess perfect majesty; I now dedicate this fragrant cloud of incense to those suffering in the cold hells, and offer food and drink in succession.
Alternatively, this medicinal incense is fragrant and exquisite, worthy of being offered to the Honored Lord.
I now present it; may you graciously accept it out of compassion. The mantra for the consecration of the medicinal food (*bhaiṣajya-bali*) is as follows:

*Āgare āgare sarvabhūtebhyo bhojyaṃ svāhā.* This mantra is universally applicable to all three families (*trikula*). After the meal, one should recite this mantra before reciting the mantra one maintains.
Offer this food with mantras.

By offering this food, one attains the joy of the Dharma; through the flavor of meditative rapture and liberation, may it be dedicated to the realm of hungry ghosts, raining down everywhere the most subtle and wondrous [nourishment].
This divine nectar-food—by partaking of this consecrated food, all shall be fully satisfied;
forever free from the suffering of hunger and thirst, and the evil karma of stinginess and greed. [The Method for Offering Food.]
First, smear fragrant paste upon the ground and sprinkle it with water;
afterwards, spread out various leaves.
One should then wash the hands, rinse the mouth, and swallow water.
Next, the food was served.
First, the food for Śāṭhika was set down,
followed by the round-rooted and long-rooted fruits.
Next, serve the various gruels;
next, serve the soups and stews;
next, serve the drinks.
Next, offer milk and curd.
Regarding the sequence of offering lamps:
perhaps it is that the lamp can dispel obstacles.
Yet it purifies drowsiness;
I now offer this. Out of compassion, please graciously accept this lamp.
The mantra is: Oṃ āloka-ya āloka-ya sarva-bhūti-jāta-prabodhaya svāhā. Having recited this mantra, [proceed].
Next, recite the root mantra; following the mantra,
perform the purification rite in order to eliminate all faults.
By offering lamps, one attains the five eyes; Thus, as the lamp of Prajñā, they illuminate the asuras.
They forever sever deceitful minds, anger, and delusion, as well as the love of strife;
They end the oppression of whipping and beating among animals.
Harming and devouring one another— May they attain a heart of loving-kindness and compassion,
And always be reborn on the paths of humans and devas. Without attachment to the realms of desire or formlessness,
May they be liberated from these fetters of delusion through samādhi.
Next, form the seal of the vast Amoghamani offering:
join the two hands in the vajra-palms gesture;
interlace the two index fingers so they resemble the shape of a jewel.
By holding both thumbs upright, it is accomplished.
Then, recite the offering mantra:
*Oṃ āmoghapūjāmaṇi padma vairocana tathāgata vilokite samanta prasara hūṃ*. This is the Great Amoghamani Offering Dhāraṇī.
Upon reciting it three times, one immediately accomplishes the assembly of such-and-such a Tathāgata,
and immeasurable, vast offerings rain down throughout boundless lands as numerous as atoms of dust.
That is to say: oceans of clouds of various kinds of unguents;
oceans of clouds of various kinds of flower garlands;
oceans of clouds of various kinds of burning incense.
Oceans of clouds of various kinds of exquisite celestial food and drink;
oceans of clouds of various kinds of exquisite celestial garments;
oceans of clouds of various kinds of mani-jewel luminous lamps and candles.
Oceans of clouds of various banners, pennants, precious canopies, and jeweled parasols;
oceans of clouds of various sublime celestial music,
throughout the assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
This constitutes a truly vast and authentic offering;
by performing the offering through the binding of mudrās and the recitation of mantras,
one obtains an immeasurable accumulation of merit.
Like space, it is without limit; in every lifetime,
one is constantly born within the great assemblies of all Tathāgatas,
arising by transformation from a lotus and attaining the five supernormal powers.
Manifesting ten billion emanations,
he is able to rescue suffering sentient beings within defiled worlds.
They shall all bring about peace, happiness, and benefit;
they will receive immeasurable karmic rewards in this very life and,
in the future, attain birth in a pure land.
I offer this *argha* perfumed water to realize the wisdom of equality and attain the rank of Dharma King over the three realms;
may these poured-down vajra-moon dew-drops be bestowed in return to drench and nourish those who dwell within the waters.
Forever departing from the realm of animals, may they swiftly attain the pure Dharma-body; reaching down even to the Avīci hell,
may all the instruments of suffering in every hell be crushed like dust and become pools of cool clarity.
May all sentient beings suffering in the realms of misery be liberated and reborn in the Pure Land.
Next, offer the argha water while reciting the refuge formula.
Joining the palms, place them upon the crown of the head.
Contemplate the true merits of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
with utmost sincerity, pay homage to and praise the Buddha.
Next, praise the Dharma and the Saṅgha, and then praise Avalokiteśvara.
Next, he praised the Great Compassionate World-Savior, the Greatly Powerful Vajra, with a verse:
"O World-Honored One of Great Compassion, who skillfully guides all through omniscience."
Ocean of merit from blessings and wisdom, I now prostrate in homage.
The Dharma of True Suchness and Śamatha, Which can purify the poisons of greed and hatred And effectively eliminate all evil destinies— I now prostrate in homage.
The Sangha who have attained liberation through the Dharma, The Sangha who dwell well in the stages of training,
the supreme field of merit— I now prostrate with my head to the Great Compassionate One, Avalokiteśvara, Who is praised by all Buddhas.
Capable of generating manifold merit, I now prostrate to the body of great power and wrath.
Excellent, O King of Vidyādharas, you who subdue those difficult to subdue; I now prostrate to you.
Having thus offered this reverent praise to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
one should likewise join the palms and, with a most earnest and respectful mind,
praise the marks and excellences (*lakṣaṇa-vyañjana*) and meritorious virtues of all other Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Regarding the verses of praise,
one should employ the eulogistic stanzas spoken by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
one should not compose such praises oneself.
The practitioner, at the three periods of each day,
should constantly recite this praise of the Buddha’s merits to awaken [the mind] of the Tathāgata [named] So-and-so, so that he will not abandon his compassionate vows.
Immeasurable light shines upon and touches the practitioner,
whereby all heavy karmic obstructions and grave offenses are completely extinguished;
body and mind become peaceful and blissful, realizing tranquil joy.
One will not grow weary while sitting for long periods in recitation;
the mind will attain purity, and one will swiftly realize samādhi.
The mantra of the Pure Jewel of the Buddha Family is as follows:
Oṃ ābhokṣamijaye svasti siddhārthe svāhā. With the right hand, press the tip of the ring finger with the thumb.
Straighten the middle fingers and slightly bend the little fingers;
press the tips of the index fingers against the sides of the upper joints of the middle fingers.
Do the same with the left hand.
Furthermore, holding a vajra with the left hand and grasping a rosary with the right hand,
he addressed [the deity], saying:
I, [Name], now reverently receive upon the crown of my head all the infinite treasuries of the Prajñāpāramitā and the myriad dharmas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
henceforth, may all Buddhas of the ten directions [behold me].
"I respectfully receive this Dharma.
Having spoken these words,
he immediately raised both hands to his head in reverent veneration.
This method of practice is called the rite of receiving and upholding with veneration and respect upon the crown of the head.
Regarding the mantra for holding the *akṣamālā* (rosary) in the Buddha Family:
employ the aforementioned rosary mudrā and recite it according to each respective family.
When reciting mantras, place the rosary at your heart. When holding the rosary, do not raise or lower it;
keep your head slightly bowed. With a sincere mind, prostrate to the Triple Gem, and then prostrate to the Eight Great Bodhisattvas.
Next, having paid homage to the retinue of the Vidyārāja, one should recite the King of Mantras with right mindfulness as if facing him before one's eyes.
If, during this time, there should be coughing, mental dullness, or forgetting the mantra, [one must correct these].
He immediately rose and went to the water to perform the ritual of sprinkling for purification (*ācamana*).
He then took the lotus-seed rosary and placed it in his hands;
with both hands cupping the beads, he joined his palms in *añjali*.
Like the shape of an unopened lotus flower,
empower it seven times with the mantra of the thousand-turn rosary.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajraguhyarājabhaṭṭāraka hūṃ. Having performed the consecration with this mantra:
He then took up the jewel, placed it upon his head, and made this aspiration:
"May all sentient beings attain their sought-after, supreme mundane and supramundane great aspirations."
One will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Recite one hundred and eight times,
holding [the object] with both hands at the heart.
Curl the five fingers of each hand like unopened lotus buds;
hold a jewel with the left hand and move the jewel with the thumb and index finger of the right hand.
Recite the mantra once;
as the sound of the word "svāhā" concludes, move one bead.
The sound of the rosary should be neither too slow nor too hurried.
Neither too high nor too low,
one should not make a sound while reciting the syllables of the mantra.
Make each detail clearly manifest.

With the mind, visualize this pure land produced by samādhi, and the image of the Buddha [named] so-and-so—previously invited—who stands within the mandala with all physical marks and signs perfectly complete.
When the practice of contemplation is thus clear and distinct,
focus intently on the recitation without allowing for interruption.
Remain free from distraction throughout the entire session of recitation.
Whether one hundred or one thousand times, if it does not reach one hundred and eight recitations, the number required for the prayer is not fulfilled.
However, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata [Name],
one’s body and mind shall become pure.
Even as they open and close their eyes,
they constantly see such-and-such a Tathāgata,
and within that meditative concentration, they hear the preaching of the profound and wondrous Dharma.
In each and every syllable and each and every phrase,
one awakens to immeasurable gates of samādhi, immeasurable gates of dhāraṇī, and immeasurable gates of liberation.
This body becomes identical to that of such-and-such a bodhisattva.
One will swiftly reach that land.
When the recitation count is completed,
hold the rosary in one's hands and, placing it upon the crown of the head, make this aspiration:
May all sentient beings be born in the world of [Name], behold the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Next,
bind the seal of concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*).
Then one contemplates the bodhicitta within the body, pure,
bright, and perfectly luminous like the full moon.
One then further reflects:
The essence of bodhicitta is free from all things;
it is free from the aggregates, elements, and sense bases, and free from the grasper and the grasped,
because of the selflessness of phenomena.
The single characteristic is equality,
for the mind is fundamentally unarisen and empty by its own nature.
Thereupon, one visualizes the syllable *Hrīḥ* upon a perfectly pure lunar disc.
From the syllable, immeasurable rays of light stream forth.
Within each and every ray of light,
one visualizes the assembly of noble ones of a specific world-system.
Surrounded by [the assembly] of such-and-such a Buddha,
as extensively described in the sūtras of that particular division;
having thus performed the recitation and cultivated samādhi.
If one wishes to exit the maṇḍala, one should form the mudrā of the principal deity,
recite the root dhāraṇī seven times,
and then release the mudrā over the crown of the head.
Then he recited this praise:
"To all the Tathāgatas present before me, to the Bodhisattvas who save the world,
who maintain the uninterrupted teaching of the Mahāyāna, and who have attained the most excellent state."
May the assembly of noble deities definitively bear witness to me;
thus, one should form the seal of universal offering and recite the mantra of the Great Amoghapāśa Jewel Offering.
Again, offer argha water and declare all the aspirations held in your heart to the assembly of noble ones:
"I pray only that the Noble Ones do not transgress their original vows, but may fulfill my wishes."
Having thus made this vow,
one prostrates at the western gate and says:
"I look up to you with reverence and offer my humble thanks."
Now, in this assembly, various ritual matters are being performed;
the incense, flowers, food, and drink are all not in accordance with the Dharma.
We feel ashamed before the noble assembly and pray that you will, out of great compassion, grant us your blessings and joy.
Having thus performed the recitation, offerings, and made the aspiration,
one should immediately form the previously mentioned fire-enclosure mudrā and rotate it once counter-clockwise.
Having completed the binding of the objects of the samaya,
may all the noble ones depart as they please. Then,
release the previously bound seal of the precious chariot.
With the two thumbs pointing outward,
push against the tips of the two middle fingers while reciting the root mantra.
To escort the assembly of noble ones,
one should form the samaya mudrās of the three families and recite their respective mantras three times each.
Then, perform the seal for donning the armor to protect the body.
Seal the five places of the body and,
before the presence of the deity, make a vow with sincere devotion.
Having paid homage to the Buddha and recited his name,
depart from the maṇḍala. Proceed outside as you wish to perform walking meditation (caṅkrama),
and there you should recite the sūtras of your own particular division.
With a mind of resolute intention (*adhyāśaya*),
one should diligently perform recitation,
sealing the Buddha, sealing the stūpa, and sealing the wall.
Joyfully practicing generosity, observing the precepts, and cultivating patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—
dedicating all such cultivated roots of goodness,
may they, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Pure Land through the highest grade of the highest birth.
Having realized the Stage of Joy (pramuditā-bhūmi),
one obtains the prophecy of unsurpassed bodhi.
This is the invocation for the dhāraṇī.
I respectfully invoke the youth Paśina to transmit this incense smoke to his disciples and entreat all Buddhas throughout world-systems as numerous as the atoms of empty space.
The seven Buddhas of the past: the Tathāgata Vipaśyin Buddha;
the fifty-three Buddhas: the Tathāgata Samantaraśmi;
and the thirty-five Buddhas: Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
The twenty-five Buddhas of the Assemblage of Jewels Tathāgatas;
the twelve divisions of the honored sūtras of the Pitaka of the Ocean of Sūtras; the Honored Dharma of Prajñā; and the various great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and Mahāsthāmaprāpta;
the Bodhisattvas of Great Compassion and the Vidyārājas of the Five Families;
the Golden Wheel King of Sovereign Power and the twenty-eight divisions.
Guhyapada Vajragarbha-rāja,
who does not abandon compassion, bear witness for this disciple;
as well as the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and arhats of the four fruits.
The Four Great Heavenly Kings; the Great Lion King who holds mantras from the thirty-six kingdoms;
the Maṇi Peacock King; the Kapiśa and Kambila Kings; the King who holds mantras to pacify the kingdom; and the King of the Path of the Mind.
The King of the Heaven of Maheśvara, the King of the Piśācas,
the Great Generals of the twenty-eight classes of spirits and ghosts,
and the Dharma-protecting King Aṭavaka.
Great General of the Summit of Mount Sumeru,
commander of the divine generals of the Five Peaks who ride flying wheels and brandish whirling swords,
descend to this sacred site to receive the incense offerings of your disciples. We entreat you to do so.
For the sake of his disciples, he shook heaven and moved earth;
above, he spread a celestial net, and below, he spread an iron mesh,
gathering in the heavenly Māras, non-Buddhists, ghosts, and spirits.
Entrust this to the Vighna messengers:
those who are currently within the boundary must be swiftly gathered in;
those outside the boundary shall not be allowed entry. Thus it is said three times. Disciple, with a single-minded heart, make this request.
The twenty-eight Vajragarbha Kings:
the Great Wheel Vajra Mañjuśrī-vajra,
the Great Ucchuṣma-vajra, and the Great Crusher Vajra.
The Vajra of the Fire-Head, the Blue-Faced Vajra,
the Vajra of the Roar (Ṭāha), the Vajra of Desire (Śveta),
the Vajra of Sharp Fangs and Claws, and the Vajra that Wounds Kṣetra.
Each leading fifty thousand yakṣas who fly on wheels and run with swords,
they gathered like clouds at the site of practice to receive the offerings made according to the disciples' hearts.
Thereafter, augment the power of the disciple.
May the mantras be fulfilled according to their wishes and swiftly attain accomplishment.
We invoke the Eastern Heavenly King, Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
He secures the realm of the East.
He respectfully invites the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka of the South and secures the realm of the South.
I respectfully invoke Virūpākṣa, the Heavenly King of the Western Quarter,
to secure the boundaries of the west.
I respectfully invoke Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of the Northern Quarter.
He secured the northern boundary.
He invited the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven from above to secure the upper boundary.
I respectfully entreat the Earth-Axis Heavenly King of the lower direction to firmly secure the boundaries of the lower direction.
May the Heavenly Kings of the six directions swiftly seize and hold the boundaries of the six directions,
so that celestial Māras, non-Buddhists, ghosts, and spirits may not enter or exit at will.
Should anyone enter or exit at will,
they shall be handed over to the Fire-Head Vajra,
who shall seize his vajra and crush their body into fine dust.
May [the head] be split into seven pieces like the branch of a pear tree.
With the urgency of the *dhāraṇī*,
this is the boundary-binding mantra of the Four Heavenly Kings.
Recite this once with a single breath three times:
*gintā gintā saṃgintā tiṣṭha*.
Now, I bind the *gintā* net in the four directions.
I have not permitted you to transcribe this.
If you are a disciple who practices this rite, you should recite it three times.

This *Yakushi Nyorai Kan-gyō Giki* (Ritual Manual for the Contemplative Practice of the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru) was completed by Shin-gen in the year of Kō-hō, Kanoe-tora (1650), and again revised in the year of Tenmei, Kanoto-usagi (1781).

Copied from the original manuscript of Eshin-in, Uji, by Jichien Jinin. Revised and collated against the aforementioned manuscript in the eighth month of autumn, the second year of the Kenpō era (1764).
Recorded by the śramaṇa Kaidō, a resident student at Ōzanji.
First proofread and annotated completed on the tenth day of the fourth month of the third year of the Kenpō era (1765) by Jishun.
